name: Investigate a complaint with 8D
description: Work through a customer complaint step by step with the 8D method and document it as a report.
input:
SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – entirely fictional, for trying things out only.

Customer: Example Automotive Inc., South plant
Part: plastic housing G-220 (PA6-GF30, injection moulded), batch 24-117, delivered on 12 March, 4,000 pieces
Complaint of 18 March: snap-fit hooks break off during assembly. The customer checked 2,000 parts, 46 are
defective (2.3 %). They require containment actions within 24 hours and an 8D report within 10 days.

Internal information:
- Batch 24-117 was produced on machine SG-4 with a newly reworked mould (maintenance on 5 March).
- The material came from a new delivery; the drying time was cut from 4 to 2.5 hours because of time pressure.
- Outgoing inspection checks dimensions and appearance according to a sampling plan, but no mechanical load on the hooks.
- Stock: 1,200 parts from batch 24-117 and 3,000 parts from batch 24-121 (same mould, normal drying).
- There were no comparable complaints in the past 12 months.

guide.problem: Complaints call for fast containment and a sound root-cause analysis. The 8D method defines the steps; the workflow works through them in a structured way and documents them consistently. It also checks whether the defect has happened before: a cause that comes back means an earlier corrective action did not work, and that belongs in the report.
guide.flow: A sequential chain: the first agent describes the problem and the containment actions (D1 to D3). The second searches the company's past 8D reports for comparable cases and looks for the causes of occurrence and non-detection (D4), stating whether a cause is a repeat or new. The third plans corrective and preventive actions (D5 to D7). The report agent compiles everything into a structured 8D report. A decision node checks the severity: in critical cases an extra agent plans the emergency containment for the next 24 hours. Before the report goes to the customer, a person releases it.
guide.input: The customer's complaint with part, batch, defect and defect rate, plus known internal information on production, material and inspection. You can also attach the complaint letter, measurement data and photos of the defect as files; the sample files contain a fictional complaint letter (PDF) and measurements (Excel). The past 8D reports come from the knowledge collection; a fictional archive of four closed reports is included.
guide.result: A structured 8D report with one field each for D1 to D8 and a list of open points the team still has to clarify; the root-cause analysis names the past reports it used. After approval, the run saves the report as a PDF and as an editable Word file. This closes the learning loop: the report agent proposes the finished 8D report for knowledge, a person decides whether it is stored, and stored reports end up in the same collection as the past reports, so the root-cause analysis finds them in future cases.
guide.adapt: Replace the test data with your complaint and attach inspection records, drawings or photos directly. Replace the fictional past reports in the knowledge collection with your own closed 8D reports (Markdown, PDF or Word); clear headings with part, defect and cause per report make the search more precise. If you use your own form, adjust the fields of the report agent under “Output format”.
guide.control: Automatic: the decision node adds the emergency containment only when the problem description marks the case as critical; the root-cause analysis decides which past reports are relevant and cites them, so every reference can be checked. There are no loops; each step runs once. A person decides twice: before files are created, someone releases the 8D report (rejecting it stops the run without files), and a person decides whether the finished report is stored as knowledge. The report remains a draft until it is released.
guide.why: 8D prescribes a fixed order in which each discipline builds on the previous one, so a sequential chain fits better than an orchestrator; only the emergency containment depends on the case and is therefore a branch. The past reports are searchable knowledge instead of text in the prompt: the archive grows with every stored case, the search brings only the relevant passages, and citations show where a repeat cause comes from. A review loop was deliberately left out, because the release by a person at the end checks the whole report anyway.

problem.name: Problem description D1–D3
problem.description: Describes the team, the problem (is/is not) and the containment actions.
problem.system: You are a quality engineer who leads 8D teams. Work on steps D1 to D3: propose a cross-functional team with roles, describe the problem precisely using 5W2H and an is/is-not analysis, and define containment actions (blocking, sorting, replacement delivery, informing the customer). For each containment action, state how its effectiveness is checked.
problem.task:
Work on D1 to D3 for this complaint:

{{run.input}}

fields.analysis: D1 to D3 as text: team, problem description (5W2H, is/is not) and containment actions with effectiveness checks
fields.critical: true if the case is critical: safety or legal relevance, a stopped customer line or affected stock that is still being shipped

root_cause.name: Root-cause analysis D4
root_cause.description: Searches past 8D reports and looks for the causes of occurrence and non-detection with 5 Whys.
root_cause.system:
You are an expert in root-cause analysis in manufacturing. Work on D4: analyse separately why the defect occurred and why it was not detected. Use a 5-Why chain for each and draw on the facts of the complaint. Rate how well each cause is supported and name tests or checks that verify it.

Before you settle on causes, search the company's past 8D reports with the search tool, using the part, the material, the defect pattern and the suspected causes as search terms. Cite every past report you use with its number. Begin your answer with a short section “Past 8D reports” that states what the search found. If a past case is comparable, compare it point by point and decide: is it the same cause (a repeat cause) or only a similar symptom with a new cause? For a repeat cause, check whether the corrective and preventive actions of the old report were implemented for this part and this machine, and say whether they failed, were not sustained, were never rolled out here, or whether the data does not allow a decision. If the past reports contain nothing comparable, say so and treat the cause as new. Never assume a match without evidence: the same customer or a similar part alone is not a repeat cause.

actions.name: Action planning D5–D7
actions.description: Plans corrective actions, their verification and prevention.
actions.system: You are a quality manager. Work on D5 to D7: define permanent corrective actions for each verified or likely cause, describe how their effectiveness will be proven, and derive preventive actions that stop similar defects in other products, for example updates to the FMEA, the control plan or work instructions. Name owners as roles and realistic dates.
actions.task:
Plan D5 to D7 based on this root-cause analysis:

{{node:root_cause}}

report.name: 8D report
report.description: Compiles all steps into a structured 8D report.
report.system: You write 8D reports for customers. Summarise the results of the previous steps completely and factually without adding new facts. Check that the steps fit together, and list contradictions or causes that are not yet verified as open points. D8 contains a closing note that recognises the team and states what is still missing before closure.

fields.d3_containment: D3 containment actions with effectiveness check
fields.d4_root_causes: D4 causes of occurrence and non-detection
fields.open_points: Open points and assumptions not yet verified

containment.name: Emergency containment
containment.description: Plans the containment for the next 24 hours in critical cases.
containment.system: You are the quality manager on call. For a critical complaint, plan the containment for the next 24 hours: block and sort all suspect stock and batches, secure deliveries in transit, arrange a 100 % inspection or a replacement delivery and inform the customer with a clear status. Name a responsible role, a deadline and how its effectiveness is checked for every action, and list what remains open.

release.name: Release report
release.instructions: Check that the 8D report only contains verified facts, that unresolved causes are marked as open and that the containment actions are realistic. Only then release it for sending to the customer.

documents.label: Complaint documents
documents.description: Optional: the complaint letter (PDF, Word), measurement data (Excel, CSV) or photos of the defect (PNG, JPEG, WebP), up to 8 files. Without files, the text applies.

# Complaint no. R-2026-031

**From:** Example Automotive Inc., South plant, incoming inspection

**To:** Quality management, supplier of plastic housings

**Date:** 18 March 2026

## Affected part

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Part | Plastic housing G-220 (PA6-GF30) |
| Batch | 24-117 |
| Delivery date | 12 March 2026 |
| Quantity delivered | 4,000 pieces |

## Description of the defect

During assembly, the snap-fit hooks on the housings break off as soon as the cover is clipped on. We checked 2,000 parts; 46 parts are defective (2.3 %). The fracture surfaces look brittle.

## Our requirements

1. Containment actions within 24 hours, including sorting of the stock at our site.
2. An 8D report within 10 days.
3. A statement on which other batches may be affected.

Contact: Ms Erica Sample, supplier quality (fictional)

past_reports.content:
# Past 8D reports – Plastiform Ltd. (fictional)

SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – entirely fictional, for trying things out only.

Archive of closed 8D reports of the quality department. One section per report.

## 8D-2024-019 – Housing G-180: snap-fit hooks break

- **Customer:** Example Automotive Inc., North plant
- **Opened / closed:** 10 September 2024 / 22 November 2024
- **Part:** plastic housing G-180 (PA6-GF30), batch 23-412, injection moulding machine SG-2
- **D2 Problem:** snap-fit hooks broke off during assembly; 1.6 % of 3,000 checked parts; brittle fracture surfaces.
- **D4 Occurrence:** the granulate was not dried enough. The dew-point sensor of dryer TR-2 was faulty; residual moisture measured afterwards: 0.35 % (limit 0.20 %). The moisture damaged the polymer during processing and reduced the toughness of the hooks. Verified with a moulding trial: wet granulate 39 N, dried granulate 60 N pull-out force.
- **D4 Non-detection:** outgoing inspection checked dimensions and appearance only; the hooks were never tested mechanically.
- **D5 Corrective actions:** sensor replaced; residual moisture measured before every batch start and recorded on the batch card (limit 0.20 %); minimum drying time of 4 hours at 80 °C fixed in work instruction AA-07 for machine SG-2.
- **D6 Verification:** ten batches in a row with pull-out forces of at least 55 N; no further complaints.
- **D7 Prevention:** pull-out test (5 parts per batch, minimum 45 N) added to the control plan of G-180. Rolling out the moisture measurement and AA-07 to all machines that process PA6: **open at closure**, due Q1 2025, owner: production manager.
- **Lesson learned:** drying is a special process; shortening the drying time needs the approval of quality management.

## 8D-2025-004 – Cover D-40: colour deviation

- **Customer:** Sample Household Appliances Ltd.
- **Part:** cover D-40 (PP, light grey), batch 25-033
- **D2 Problem:** covers too dark, colour difference ΔE 2.4 (limit 1.0).
- **D4 Occurrence:** the masterbatch dosing unit was not recalibrated after a change of masterbatch supplier. **Non-detection:** colour checked by eye without a reference sample under standard light.
- **D5–D7:** calibration after every masterbatch change; colour measured with a colorimeter at every batch start; reference samples at all PP machines. Closed in March 2025.

## 8D-2025-012 – Clip holder H-12: wrong carton labels

- **Customer:** Example Automotive Inc., North plant
- **D2 Problem:** cartons of clip holder H-12 carried the label of H-14.
- **D4 Occurrence:** the label template was chosen by hand at the packing station; the two part numbers look alike. **Non-detection:** no comparison between production order and label.
- **D5–D7:** barcode scan compares production order and label before every carton is closed. Closed in July 2025.

## 8D-2025-021 – Trim strip L-300: scratches on the visible surface

- **Customer:** Sample Household Appliances Ltd.
- **Part:** trim strip L-300 (PC/ABS)
- **D2 Problem:** scratches on the visible surface on arrival; 4 % of the parts.
- **D4 Occurrence:** after a packaging change to save costs, the strips were packed without separators and rubbed against each other during transport. **Non-detection:** the final inspection takes place before packing.
- **D5–D7:** back to separator trays; transport test for every packaging change. Closed in October 2025.
